sentences.en: Harold had fallen, as his valiant brothers had fallen before him.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德倒下了，正如他那些英勇的兄弟们此前倒下一样。

sentences.en: The event too truly showed that England had fallen with the sons of Godwin, that as ever in this age, everything turned on the life of one man,
sentences.zh: 这一事件确实表明，随着戈德温家族子嗣的陨落，英格兰也随之陷落了；正如那个时代一贯的情况，一切都系于一人之身，

sentences.en: and that the one man who could have guarded and saved England was taken from her.
sentences.zh: 而那个唯一能守护并拯救英格兰的人，却被从她身边夺走了。

sentences.en: Such being the case, it is from that memorable day that we may fairly date the overthrow,
sentences.zh: 既然如此，我们完全可以从那个值得纪念的日子算起，标志着覆灭的开始，

sentences.en: what we know to have been only the imperfect and temporary overthrow of our ancient and free Teutonic England.
sentences.zh: 我们所知的，那不过是我们古老而自由的条顿英格兰不完整且暂时的覆灭。

sentences.en: In the eyes of men of the next generation, that day was the fatal day of England, the day of the sad overthrow of our dear country, the day of her handing over to foreign lords.
sentences.zh: 在下一代人眼中，那一天是英格兰的致命之日，是我们亲爱的国家悲惨覆灭之日，是她被移交给外国领主之日。

sentences.en: From that day forward the Normans began to work the will of God upon the folk of England, till there were left in England no chiefs of the land of English blood,
sentences.zh: 从那天起，诺曼人开始在英格兰人民身上施行上帝的旨意，直到英格兰再无英格兰血统的领主，

sentences.en: till all were brought down to bondage and to sorrow, till it was a shame to be called an Englishman, and the men of England were no more a people.
sentences.zh: 直到所有人都陷入奴役与悲哀，直到被称为英格兰人成为一种耻辱，英格兰人不再是一个民族。

sentences.en: So that was one of the great historians.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是其中一位伟大的历史学家。

sentences.en: It was Edward A.
sentences.zh: 他是爱德华·A·

sentences.en: Freeman.
sentences.zh: 弗里曼。

sentences.en: It was the man with whom, 10 episodes ago, we began our account of the Norman ConqueSt.
sentences.zh: 就是我们在十集前开始讲述诺曼征服史时提到的那个人。

sentences.en: Now, you can't argue with Edward A.
sentences.zh: 现在，你无法反驳爱德华·A·

sentences.en: Freeman because he was Regis Professor of History at Oxford.
sentences.zh: 弗里曼，因为他是牛津大学的雷吉斯历史学教授。

sentences.en: His book on the Norman Conquest, the history of the Norman Conquest in England, not just the best, but more importantly, the longest history of the Norman Conquest at six volumes,
sentences.zh: 他关于诺曼征服的著作——《诺曼征服英格兰史》，不仅是最好的，更重要的是，它是篇幅最长的诺曼征服史，足足有六卷，

sentences.en: published to mark the 800th anniversary.
sentences.zh: 是为了纪念（征服）800周年而出版的。

sentences.en: And he correctly identified the Normans as the absolute filth of Europe and England and its Teutonic traditions and its traditions of freedom and democracy and love of country.
sentences.zh: 他准确地将诺曼人认定为欧洲和英格兰的绝对败类，摧毁了英格兰的条顿传统，以及其自由、民主和爱国传统。

sentences.en: He identified those, Tom, as the motor of all history.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他认定这些才是所有历史的驱动力。

sentences.en: And what is more, he pointed out quite rightly that it doesn't matter about the masses in history and millions of people.
sentences.zh: 而且更重要的是，他非常正确地指出，历史中的大众和千百万人并不重要。

sentences.en: It's really about one man.
sentences.zh: 真正重要的是一个人。

sentences.en: And that man is Harold Godwinson, the one man who could have guarded and saved England.
sentences.zh: 那个人就是哈罗德·戈德温森，那个唯一能守护并拯救英格兰的人。

sentences.en: This is the best episode of the rest of the history we've ever done.
sentences.zh: 这是我们做过的所有历史节目中最好的一集。

sentences.en: But are you going to now say that this is all tosh and rubbish?
sentences.zh: 但你现在是要说这一切都是胡言乱语吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So I'm very much your kind of guy.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常欣赏你这类人。

sentences.en: He loves Harold Godwinson.
sentences.zh: 他热爱哈罗德·戈德温森。

sentences.en: He writes enormously long books and just go on and on and on and never stop.
sentences.zh: 他写了极其冗长的书，没完没了，永不停歇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Very much your kind of guy.
sentences.zh: 非常欣赏你这类人。

sentences.en: So clearly he is mourning the death of Harold.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，他在哀悼哈罗德的死。

sentences.en: He sees the two as being, you know, interfused.
sentences.zh: 他认为这两者是，你知道的，交织在一起的。

sentences.en: Harold is the one man who could have guarded and saved England and now he is dead.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德是唯一能守护并拯救英格兰的人，而现在他死了。

sentences.en: So is he right that Hastings was a catastrophe for England?
sentences.zh: 那么，他认为黑斯廷斯对英格兰来说是一场灾难，这正确吗？

sentences.en: I mean, did it result in the extinction of her ancestral freedoms?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是否导致了英格兰祖传自由的灭绝？

sentences.en: Was everything that Anglo-Saxon England had been destroyed at Senlach Hill?
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰的一切是否都在森拉克山被摧毁了？

sentences.en: Do you know who'd agreed with this bloke?
sentences.zh: 你知道谁会同意这家伙的观点吗？

sentences.en: Freeman.
sentences.zh: 弗里曼。

sentences.en: The roundheads.
sentences.zh: 圆颅党人。

sentences.en: People in the 17th century who believed in the Norman yoke.
sentences.zh: 17世纪那些相信“诺曼枷锁”的人。

sentences.en: Dominic, we will be coming to that.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们稍后会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: We'll be doing a bonus on the way that 1066 and the Norman Conquest was interpreted.
sentences.zh: 我们会做一个关于1066年和诺曼征服如何被解读的特别节目。

sentences.en: So there will be more about that if you're a member of the Rest is History Club.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是《历史的余味》俱乐部的成员，会有更多相关内容。

sentences.en: But for now, we're going to try and answer some of those questions that I just put.
sentences.zh: 但现在，我们要试着回答我刚才提出的那些问题。

sentences.en: But a reminder, first of all, of where we ended the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 不过首先，提醒一下上一集我们结束的地方。

sentences.en: So it is 1654 on the 14th of October, St. Calixtus' day, 1066, and the sun has just set.
sentences.zh: 现在是1654年10月14日，1066年圣卡利克斯图斯日，太阳刚刚落山。

sentences.en: And the sun, Dominic, has also set on the fortunes of the Godwins and of England.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，太阳也落在了戈德温家族和英格兰的命运之上。

sentences.en: Oh, terrible.
sentences.zh: 噢，太可怕了。

sentences.en: The slopes and the summit of Senlach Hill are piled with the bodies of the dead and the dying, and the mud reeks of blood and emptied bowels.
sentences.zh: 森拉克山的山坡和山顶堆满了死者和垂死者的尸体，泥土里散发着血腥味和排泄物的恶臭。

sentences.en: Cries fill the darkening twilight, and already you've got to imagine pillagers creeping up through the dark,
sentences.zh: 哭喊声充斥着昏暗的黄昏，你已经可以想象掠夺者在黑暗中悄悄摸上来，

sentences.en: starting to strip corpses of their mail shirts, their weapons, their clothes, anything that might be of any value.
sentences.zh: 开始剥下尸体上的锁子甲、武器、衣服，任何可能有价值的东西。

sentences.en: And the killing is not yet over, even though darkness is now over Sussex, because the English have turned and fled.
sentences.zh: 杀戮还没有结束，尽管黑暗已经笼罩了萨塞克斯，因为英格兰人已经转身逃跑了。

sentences.en: But this, of course, is when the Norman cavalry comes into its own, because they can pursue the fugitives and hunt them down.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这正是诺曼骑兵大显身手的时候，因为他们可以追击逃兵并将他们猎杀。

sentences.en: You'll be glad to hear, Dominic, they don't have it all their own way, because it does seem, despite the garbled nature of the various accounts,
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你会很高兴听到他们并没有完全占尽上风，因为尽管各种记载含糊不清，

sentences.en: there seems confusion as to exactly what happens.
sentences.zh: 似乎对于到底发生了什么还存在困惑。

sentences.en: But it's clear that a body of English warriors, either fugitives or perhaps new arrivals, make a stand perhaps on some ancient earthworks.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，一群英格兰战士，无论是逃兵还是刚赶到的援军，在一些古老的土方工事上进行了抵抗。

sentences.en: It's not entirely clear.
sentences.zh: 这一点不太明确。

sentences.en: And they inflict a number of casualties on the Normans.
sentences.zh: 他们给诺曼人造成了一定的伤亡。

sentences.en: And there is one report that useless of Boulogne,
sentences.zh: 有报道称，布洛涅的尤斯塔斯，

sentences.en: William's mate, who, according to the earliest account we have, was actually responsible for the death of Harold, that he received a blow between his shoulders
sentences.zh: 威廉的伙伴，根据我们现有的最早记载，他实际上应对哈罗德的死负责，他肩膀之间挨了一击，

sentences.en: that led to blood gushing out from his nose and mouth in the Great Fountain.
sentences.zh: 导致鲜血从他的鼻子和嘴里喷涌而出，就像大喷泉一样。

sentences.en: That's good news.
sentences.zh: 那是个好消息。

sentences.en: That's great news.
sentences.zh: 那真是个好消息。

sentences.en: I'm very pleased to hear that.
sentences.zh: 听到这个我很高兴。

sentences.en: And there are late accounts that report an entire ditch ending up filled with Norman casualties
sentences.zh: 还有一些晚期的记载称，整个沟渠最终填满了诺曼人的尸体，

sentences.en: and that it was called the Malfoss, so the evil ditch, a great ditch that had been covered with brambles.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“恶沟”（Malfoss），那是一条被荆棘覆盖的大沟。

sentences.en: So the killing does go on through the night.
sentences.zh: 所以杀戮确实持续了一整夜。

sentences.en: But when dawn comes on the 15th of October, what it reveals is a spectacle of carnage that is so terrible that even the Normans are kind of stunned by it.
sentences.zh: 但当10月15日的黎明到来时，它展现出的屠杀景象是如此可怕，以至于连诺曼人都被惊呆了。

sentences.en: A bit like the English after Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 有点像阿金库尔战役后的英国人。

sentences.en: And we should remind ourselves that the English will go on to win a victory over the French in due course.
sentences.zh: 我们应该提醒自己，英国人最终会在适当的时候战胜法国人。

sentences.en: We had the last laugh.
sentences.zh: 我们笑到了最后。

sentences.en: William of Poitiers writes about the battlefield of Saint-Nac-Kale.
sentences.zh: 普瓦捷的威廉写到了圣纳克卡莱的战场。

sentences.en: Far and wide, the earth was covered with the flower of the English nobility and youth drenched in gore.
sentences.zh: 大地四处都覆盖着浸透鲜血的英格兰贵族和青年精英的尸体。

sentences.en: And William orders the Norman dead to be buried.
sentences.zh: 威廉下令掩埋诺曼人的尸体。

sentences.en: But does he order the English dead to be buried, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 但他下令掩埋英格兰人的尸体了吗，多米尼克？

sentences.en: He does not.
sentences.zh: 他没有。

sentences.en: He leaves them as food for worms and wolves, birds and dogs, as the Carmen puts it.
sentences.zh: 正如《卡门》诗中所写，他把他们留作了蠕虫、狼、鸟和狗的食物。

sentences.en: He does, however, give orders for the bodies of Harold and his two brothers, Girth and Leofwine, to be found.
sentences.zh: 不过，他确实下令寻找哈罗德及其两个兄弟格思和利奥夫温的尸体。

sentences.en: And they are treated with more respect, although there are so many differing stories about what happens to them and how William chooses to treat them.
sentences.zh: 他们受到了更多的尊重，尽管关于他们发生了什么以及威廉选择如何对待他们，有太多不同的说法。

sentences.en: It's actually, again, very hard to make sense of what may actually have happened.
sentences.zh: 实际上，同样很难弄清楚到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: So there is one brilliant late story that Harold's body has been left so mangled that no one can identify it.
sentences.zh: 有一个精彩的晚期故事说，哈罗德的尸体被毁坏得面目全非，没人能认出来。

sentences.en: And so they send for Edith's swan neck, his lover, mistress, concubine, first wife, whatever you want to call her.
sentences.zh: 于是他们派人去找“天鹅颈”伊迪丝，他的情人、情妇、妃子、第一任妻子，随便你怎么称呼她。

sentences.en: In the words of the chronicler, she had a more intimate knowledge of his body than anyone else.
sentences.zh: 用编年史作者的话说，她比任何人都更了解他的身体。

sentences.en: If those previous accounts in the last episode are true, then, I mean, that would avail her nothing.
sentences.zh: 如果上一集提到的那些记载是真的，那么，我的意思是，这对她毫无帮助。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, but maybe they found them as well and kind of brought them back and stuck them on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但也许他们也找到了它们，把它们带回来并拼凑在一起了。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: The Carmen, which is the source closest in time to Hastings, recounts how William has Harold's body wrapped in purple linen.
sentences.zh: 《卡门》是时间上最接近黑斯廷斯战役的史料，它讲述了威廉如何让人用紫色亚麻布包裹哈罗德的尸体。

sentences.en: And then Harold's mother, Gither, comes and offers to pay William Harold's weight in gold if she can be given the body.
sentences.zh: 然后哈罗德的母亲吉莎来了，提出如果能把尸体给她，她愿意支付哈罗德体重相当的黄金。

sentences.en: Again, a possible classical allusion there to Achilles and Hector and everything.
sentences.zh: 这又是一个可能的古典典故，让人想起阿喀琉斯和赫克托耳等等。

sentences.en: I mean, is it being modeled directly on them?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是直接模仿他们吗？

sentences.en: Is Gither thinking of that?
sentences.zh: 吉莎在想那个吗？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: But according to the Carmen, William doesn't give Gither her son's body.
sentences.zh: 但根据《卡门》，威廉并没有把她儿子的尸体交给吉莎。

sentences.en: And instead, he orders it to be buried on top of a cliff looking out over the channel.
sentences.zh: 相反，他下令将其埋葬在俯瞰海峡的悬崖顶上。

sentences.en: And somebody raises a stone, one of the Normans, and scribes on it.
sentences.zh: 有人竖起了一块石头，其中一个诺曼人，并在上面刻字。

sentences.en: By command of the duke, you repose here, King Harold, so that you may remain guardian of the shore and ocean.
sentences.zh: “奉公爵之命，你安息于此，哈罗德国王，以便你继续守护海岸与海洋。”

sentences.en: And if that's true, I mean, what's interesting is that William is being described as a duke and Harold is still being described as a king.
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的，我的意思是，有趣的是威廉被称为公爵，而哈罗德仍然被称为国王。

sentences.en: So I don't think that would have lasted very long.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这不会持续太久。

sentences.en: There are other accounts of what happens to Harold's body.
sentences.zh: 关于哈罗德尸体的下落还有其他说法。

sentences.en: So a later account says it was given to Gither, who buried it in Waltham Abbey in Essex, which Harold had refounded under his own kind of patronage in 1060.
sentences.zh: 一个较晚的记载说它被交给了吉莎，她将其埋葬在埃塞克斯的沃尔瑟姆修道院，那是哈罗德在1060年以自己的名义重新建立的。

sentences.en: So that's, I mean, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我们不知道。

sentences.en: And there is a modern theory that it's in the Sussex port of Bosham, which had been Harold's birthplace and is shown in the Bay of Tapestry.
sentences.zh: 还有一个现代理论认为它在萨塞克斯的博斯汉姆港，那是哈罗德的出生地，在贝叶挂毯中也有展示。

sentences.en: Harold sails from it for his disastrous trip to France.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德从那里启航前往法国，开启了他那灾难性的旅程。

sentences.en: So within an arrow's flight of Keith Richards's house in West Wittering.
sentences.zh: 就在西威特林基思·理查兹家的一箭之地外。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's the version I like to believe.
sentences.zh: 那是我愿意相信的版本。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I imagine Keith Richards would be interested in this.
sentences.zh: 我想基思·理查兹会对这个感兴趣。

sentences.en: Keith Richards loves his history.
sentences.zh: 基思·理查兹热爱历史。

sentences.en: So he'd have been all over the fact that in 1954, an Anglo-Saxon coffin was found in the church there.
sentences.zh: 所以他一定会关注1954年在那里的一座教堂里发现了一具盎格鲁-撒克逊棺材的事实。

sentences.en: And it apparently was the skeleton of a formidable looking warrior.
sentences.zh: 而且据称那是一具看起来威风凛凛的战士的骨架。

sentences.en: So who knows?
sentences.zh: 所以谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I think of Keith Richards because he seems to be very much an Anglo-Saxon man, not a Norman.
sentences.zh: 我想到基思·理查兹，因为他看起来非常像个盎格鲁-撒克逊人，而不是诺曼人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think Mick Jagger, more of a Norman.
sentences.zh: 我觉得米克·贾格尔更像个诺曼人。

sentences.en: Agreed.
sentences.zh: 同意。

sentences.en: Very interested in money.
sentences.zh: 对金钱非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Cold-eyed.
sentences.zh: 冷酷的眼神。

sentences.en: Cold-eyed.
sentences.zh: 冷酷的眼神。

sentences.en: But Keith Richards is very much a man who would have sported an excellent moustache in the 11th century.
sentences.zh: 但基思·理查兹绝对是那种在11世纪会留着漂亮胡子的人。

sentences.en: There are Norman accounts that the English on the night before Hastings spend it getting wasted.
sentences.zh: 有诺曼人的记载称，黑斯廷斯战役前夜，英格兰人都在喝得烂醉。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 你看，就是这样。

sentences.en: That's quite Rolling Stones.
sentences.zh: 这很滚石乐队。

sentences.en: Anyway, however, all these stories, we don't really know which of them is true.
sentences.zh: 总之，无论如何，所有这些故事，我们真的不知道哪一个是真的。

sentences.en: There's inevitably an also report that Harold survived the battle and became a hermit, which is traditional in such cases.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地还有报道称哈罗德在战斗中幸存下来并成为了一名隐士，这在类似案例中很常见。

sentences.en: But whatever, whatever the truth, he is gone.
sentences.zh: 但无论真相如何，他已经不在了。

sentences.en: And the big question that everyone presumably is asking at this point is, does this mean the war is over?
sentences.zh: 大家此时此刻可能都在问的一个大问题是，这意味着战争结束了吗？

sentences.en: Right, because it could continue, right?
sentences.zh: 对，因为战争本可以继续，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, William Ernie has the tiniest, tiniest bit of England, a little foothold.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，威廉实际上只占领了英格兰极小极小的一部分，一个小小的立足点。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of England, and England has a very sophisticated state, and it's got a lot of people, and it's got a martial tradition.
sentences.zh: 英格兰还有很大一片土地，而且英格兰拥有非常先进的国家体制，人口众多，还有尚武传统。

sentences.en: So why does – this is an interesting question – why does the Norman conquest basically – why is this game over?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么——这是一个有趣的问题——为什么诺曼征服基本上——为什么这场游戏就结束了？

sentences.en: Well, we laugh, perhaps, at the way that Victorians insist on great men, the fate of great men affecting the course of nations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们或许会嘲笑维多利亚时代的人坚持伟人论，认为伟人的命运影响着国家的进程。

sentences.en: I think in this case he's not far wrong.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这种情况下，他并没有说错。

sentences.en: I think the war absolutely could have still been prosecuted and won had there been anyone left in England competent to continue the resistance to William and, by implication,
sentences.zh: 我认为如果英格兰还有人有能力继续抵抗威廉，并暗示能被接受为国王，战争绝对是可以继续进行并获胜的，

sentences.en: be accepted as king.
sentences.zh: 被接受为国王。

sentences.en: So you need someone who's competent and can rule as a legitimate king.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要一个有能力且能作为合法国王统治的人。

sentences.en: But the problem is there isn't really anyone.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，真的没有这样的人。

sentences.en: So Geath and Leofine are dead, Edwin and Morker, if they were at the battle, nobody mentions it, they certainly haven't hung around.
sentences.zh: 格思和利奥夫温死了，埃德温和莫尔卡，如果他们参加了战斗，没人提到过，他们肯定没有留下来。

sentences.en: Whether they're coming from Hastings or whether they're coming from the Midlands, they go to London and they rescue their sister, Harold's widow, and take her away up to Chester.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是从黑斯廷斯还是从中部地区赶来，他们都去了伦敦，救出了他们的妹妹，也就是哈罗德的遗孀，把她带到了切斯特。

sentences.en: There is Edgar Atherling, who is Edward the Confessor's great nephew.
sentences.zh: 还有埃德加·艾瑟林，他是忏悔者爱德华的侄孙。

sentences.en: You know, he has the blood of the West Saxon kings in his veins, and we're told in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他身上流着西撒克逊国王的血，我们在《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》中读到过。

sentences.en: Well, Archbishop Aildred, so that's the Archbishop of York, and the people of London wish to have him as king, as indeed was his right by birth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大主教艾尔德雷德，也就是约克大主教，和伦敦人民希望他成为国王，这确实是他与生俱来的权利。

sentences.en: But, you know, he's a teenager.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他还是个少年。

sentences.en: He lacks any military resources of his own whatsoever, and he is now facing the best general in Europe who's just won a very, very bloody battle.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何自己的军事资源，而且他现在面对的是欧洲最优秀的将军，他刚刚赢得了一场非常、非常血腥的战斗。

sentences.en: So I think that when Freeman says the one man who could have guarded and saved England was taken from her, namely Harold, I mean, he's not exaggerating, really.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为当弗里曼说那个唯一能守护并拯救英格兰的人被从她身边夺走，即哈罗德，我的意思是，他真的没有夸张。

sentences.en: Had Harold survived, even the loss at Hastings might have been, you know, might not have been fatal.
sentences.zh: 如果哈罗德幸存下来，即使在黑斯廷斯的失败，你知道，可能也不会是致命的。

sentences.en: Quick question.
sentences.zh: 快速问一下。

sentences.en: Is this not the moment where Edwin and Morker could step up and claim their place in history, and actually they don't, and this was their opportunity?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是埃德温和莫尔卡挺身而出、在历史上占据一席之地的时刻吗？但他们实际上没有这样做，这难道不是他们的机会吗？

sentences.en: Maybe, but they don't.
sentences.zh: 或许吧，但他们并没有。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the salient thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这才是最突出的问题。

sentences.en: And presumably they don't because they feel they haven't got backing.
sentences.zh: 据推测，他们之所以没有这样做，是因为他们觉得没有后盾。

sentences.en: Does this mean then that William has won?
sentences.zh: 那么这是否意味着威廉已经赢了？

sentences.en: Again, not necessarily, because as you said, England is huge.
sentences.zh: 同样，不一定，因为正如你所说，英格兰太大了。

sentences.en: It has immense resources of manpower.
sentences.zh: 它拥有庞大的人力资源。

sentences.en: William's force relative to the manpower available to a native English king is small and smaller than it was when it landed because lots of people have died in the great battle.
sentences.zh: 相对于英格兰本土国王所能动用的人力，威廉的兵力很小，而且比登陆时更少了，因为在伟大的战役中很多人已经阵亡了。

sentences.en: He still has no declared allies in England, and of course winter is closing in.
sentences.zh: 他在英格兰仍然没有公开的盟友，而且冬天当然也快到了。

sentences.en: So he's still not in a secure position.
sentences.zh: 所以他仍然没有处于稳固的地位。

sentences.en: And effectively, he has to seize command of the kingdom, which means being recognized by the Witan,
sentences.zh: 实际上，他必须夺取王国的指挥权，这意味着要得到贤人会议的认可，

sentences.en: by the magnates and the leading bishops and archbishops of the kingdom before winter sets in, or he's in real trouble.
sentences.zh: 在冬天到来之前得到王国权贵以及主要主教和大主教的认可，否则他就会陷入真正的麻烦。

sentences.en: So what does he do?
sentences.zh: 那么他该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: First of all, he sits and waits for the Witan to offer him the crown.
sentences.zh: 首先，他坐等贤人会议向他献上王冠。

sentences.en: And a week passes, two weeks pass, and still there is nothing from the Witan.
sentences.zh: 一周过去了，两周过去了，贤人会议那边依然毫无动静。

sentences.en: So he decides, hang this, I'm not putting up with this.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定，去他的，我可受不了这个。

sentences.en: So he raises camp and he heads eastwards for Dover.
sentences.zh: 于是他拔营起程，向东前往多佛。

sentences.en: And on the way, he makes sure to proclaim to the English what the fruits of opposing him will be.
sentences.zh: 在路上，他确保向英格兰人宣告反抗他的后果。

sentences.en: So they go past the coastal town of Romney, where some of the Norman ships had landed by mistake and the locals had slaughtered them.
sentences.zh: 他们经过了沿海城镇罗姆尼，那里曾有一些诺曼船只误打误撞地登陆，结果被当地人屠杀殆尽。

sentences.en: And William now exacts a terrible vengeance on them by putting the town to the torch.
sentences.zh: 威廉现在通过将该镇付之一炬，对他们进行了可怕的报复。

sentences.en: He then advances on Dover, which surrenders at the very site of his army.
sentences.zh: 随后他向多佛进军，多佛在见到他军队的那一刻就投降了。

sentences.en: And so clearly, despite all the casualties that the Normans had suffered at Hastings, they're still a very, very intimidating site.
sentences.zh: 很显然，尽管诺曼人在黑斯廷斯遭受了惨重的伤亡，但他们仍然是一支非常、非常令人生畏的力量。

sentences.en: And William stays there maybe for a week.
sentences.zh: 威廉在那里待了大约一周。

sentences.en: One source says for three weeks, improving its fortifications, getting reinforcements.
sentences.zh: 有一个来源说是三周，期间他改善了防御工事，并获得了增援。

sentences.en: Dover, of course, is, you know, I mean, it's the shortest crossing, so a very useful stronghold for an invader of England to control.
sentences.zh: 多佛当然是，你知道，我的意思是，它是最短的渡口，所以对于英格兰的入侵者来说，这是一个非常有用的据点。

sentences.en: And then having secured Dover, he then goes on to secure two crucial prizes.
sentences.zh: 在稳固了多佛之后，他接着去夺取了两个关键的战利品。

sentences.en: So the first of these is Canterbury, which submits to him in person.
sentences.zh: 第一个是坎特伯雷，它亲自向他投降了。

sentences.en: So William is marching from Dover to Canterbury towards London.
sentences.zh: 威廉正从多佛经坎特伯雷向伦敦进军。

sentences.en: And Canterbury, of course, is the seat of the Archbishop of Canterbury.
sentences.zh: 坎特伯雷当然是坎特伯雷大主教的驻地。

sentences.en: So the great focus of English sacrality.
sentences.zh: 因此它是英格兰神圣性的核心所在。

sentences.en: And he also gets Winchester, which falls to a flying column of men that he sent.
sentences.zh: 他还拿下了温彻斯特，这是由他派出的机动部队攻下的。

sentences.en: And Winchester, you know, it's the capital of Alfred the Great.
sentences.zh: 温彻斯特，你知道，那是阿尔弗雷德大帝的首都。

sentences.en: It's been slightly displaced as the capital by London, but it's still a very, very significant place for the West Saxons.
sentences.zh: 虽然它作为首都的地位已被伦敦略微取代，但对于西撒克逊人来说，它仍然是一个非常、非常重要的地方。

sentences.en: And so to control that, that's a very good sign.
sentences.zh: 所以能控制那里，是一个非常好的迹象。

sentences.en: And it's all the more significant because it is now, as both Canterbury and Winchester submit to him,
sentences.zh: 而且这更具意义，因为就在坎特伯雷和温彻斯特都向他投降时，

sentences.en: that news reaches William that Edgar Atherling has been elected king by the Witton.
sentences.zh: 威廉收到了消息，埃德加·艾瑟林被贤人会议选为国王。

sentences.en: So that's a moment that's often elided in the stories of the Norman Conquest that's barely mentioned in a lot of accounts, which is that suddenly we do have an alternative king.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在诺曼征服的故事中经常被忽略的时刻，在许多记载中几乎没有提及，那就是我们突然有了另一位国王。

sentences.en: And yes, you said he was a teenager.
sentences.zh: 是的，你说过他还是个少年。

sentences.en: That said, teenagers have often won thrones before and Edmund Ironside had been a teenager when he'd been fighting Canute.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，少年也曾多次赢得王位，埃德蒙·艾恩赛德在与克努特作战时也还是个少年。

sentences.en: And William had been a teenager when stamping down resistance in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 威廉在镇压诺曼底的抵抗时也还是个少年。

sentences.en: So a lot of listeners to this would be like, well, who's this bloke?
sentences.zh: 所以很多听众可能会想，这家伙是谁？

sentences.en: I've never heard of this bloke.
sentences.zh: 我从来没听说过这家伙。

sentences.en: I mean, don't try and pretend he's a big player in this story because I've never heard of him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，别试图假装他是这个故事里的重要角色，因为我从来没听说过他。

sentences.en: And again, it's a dog that doesn't bark.
sentences.zh: 这又是一个“沉默的狗”的例子。

sentences.en: I mean, Edgar Atherling is in London, which is the great prize, which is the capital.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，埃德加·艾瑟林在伦敦，那是最大的战利品，是首都。

sentences.en: So, and actually when William marches on London from Canterbury and says surrender, London does not surrender.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上当威廉从坎特伯雷向伦敦进军并要求投降时，伦敦并没有投降。

sentences.en: So why does this story not go anywhere?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么这个故事没有下文了呢？

sentences.en: Why doesn't Edgar Atherling hold out, raise an army and then the next 10 years be a great civil war between Edgar Atherling and William?
sentences.zh: 为什么埃德加·艾瑟林不坚持抵抗，召集军队，然后接下来的10年里进行一场埃德加·艾瑟林和威廉之间的大内战呢？

sentences.en: So he's one of those kind of ambivalent kings.
sentences.zh: 所以他就是那种模棱两可的国王之一。

sentences.en: I suppose he's kind of the Anglo-Saxon Lady Jane Grey.
sentences.zh: 我想他就像是盎格鲁-撒克逊人的简·格雷夫人。

sentences.en: You're never quite sure whether to include him in the list of English kings or not.
sentences.zh: 你永远无法确定是否应该把他列入英格兰国王名单。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the answer is that clearly he lacks the charisma and the resources to meet William in the field, which is why when William marches on London,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为答案很明显，他缺乏在战场上对抗威廉的魅力和资源，这就是为什么当威廉向伦敦进军时，

sentences.en: he stays immured within the walls.
sentences.zh: 他只能躲在城墙内。

sentences.en: William occupies Southwark, so the southern stretches of the Thames, south of London Bridge, does not try and force London Bridge and enter London.
sentences.zh: 威廉占领了萨瑟克，也就是泰晤士河南岸、伦敦桥以南的地区，并没有试图强攻伦敦桥进入伦敦。

sentences.en: But he makes sure to put Southwark to the torch so that everyone in London who are around Edgar can witness the fact that this new king is powerless to resist William's advance.
sentences.zh: 但他确保将萨瑟克付之一炬，以便伦敦城内埃德加周围的所有人都能亲眼目睹这位新国王无力阻挡威廉的推进。

sentences.en: And he then carries on heading westwards into the heartlands of Wessex.
sentences.zh: 然后他继续向西前往威塞克斯的心脏地带。

sentences.en: And he adopts this policy that we've already quoted, but I'll quote it again.
sentences.zh: 他采取了我们之前引用过的政策，但我会再引用一次。

sentences.en: William of Poitiers describing the Norman way of war, striking fear by laying waste the crops, fields and domains, capturing all the towns that lay in his path,
sentences.zh: 普瓦捷的威廉描述了诺曼人的战争方式，通过摧毁庄稼、田野和领地来制造恐惧，占领沿途所有的城镇，

sentences.en: putting garrisons in them.
sentences.zh: 并在其中驻扎守军。

sentences.en: In short, to assault a given region relentlessly and engulf it in a great multitude of troubles.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，就是无情地攻击某个地区，使其陷入巨大的苦难之中。

sentences.en: And this is now the fate that is visited on Wessex, which is the heartland of England, of course.
sentences.zh: 这就是现在降临在威塞克斯身上的命运，当然，那是英格兰的心脏地带。

sentences.en: It's the kingdom that had been ruled by Alfred and by Athelstan.
sentences.zh: 那是曾由阿尔弗雷德和阿塞尔斯坦统治的王国。

sentences.en: And it was the great stronghold of the Godwins.
sentences.zh: 它也是戈德温家族的伟大据点。

sentences.en: Harold had been Earl of Wessex.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德曾是威塞克斯伯爵。

sentences.en: And so William is making, you know, he is rubbing the noses of the English in the fact that the heartbeat of the English kingdom is now his to do with as he pleases.
sentences.zh: 所以威廉正在，你知道，他正在让英格兰人难堪，因为英格兰王国的核心现在任由他摆布。

sentences.en: And so he ravages the whole way westwards as far as Wallingford in Oxfordshire.
sentences.zh: 于是他一路向西劫掠，直到牛津郡的沃灵福德。

sentences.en: And as the name of Wallingford suggests, it's a fortified ford across the Thames.
sentences.zh: 正如沃灵福德这个名字所暗示的那样，它是泰晤士河上一个设防的浅滩。

sentences.en: Alfred had built walls around it.
sentences.zh: 阿尔弗雷德曾在它周围筑墙。

sentences.en: It was one of his kind of fortified burrs.
sentences.zh: 它是他那种设防堡垒之一。

sentences.en: But the local thane surrenders it to William.
sentences.zh: 但当地的领主把它交给了威廉。

sentences.en: You know, he's just one glimpse of William at the head of his army and he's, hey, please come in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他只是瞥见威廉率领军队，就说，嘿，请进。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not hanging around here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可不想在这里逗留。

sentences.en: And so William occupies Wallingford and it is there that he receives a key submission.
sentences.zh: 于是威廉占领了沃灵福德，就在那里他接受了一个关键的投降。

sentences.en: And this is Stigand, the Archbishop of Canterbury.
sentences.zh: 这就是坎特伯雷大主教斯蒂甘德。

sentences.en: And that must be a big moment because Stigand brings the authority and the legitimacy of the English church.
sentences.zh: 那一定是一个重要的时刻，因为斯蒂甘德带来了英格兰教会的权威和合法性。

sentences.en: Well, bear in mind that Stigand is a very controversial figure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，要记住斯蒂甘德是一个非常有争议的人物。

sentences.en: The fact that he is simultaneously the Bishop of Winchester has been used as one of the reasons for why William should be given a papal banner.
sentences.zh: 他同时担任温彻斯特主教的事实，已被用作威廉应该获得教皇旗帜的原因之一。

sentences.en: So the fact that Stigand, who knows that he is in the crosshairs of William, that he chooses to surrender is, I think, doubly significant.
sentences.zh: 所以，深知自己处于威廉打击目标的斯蒂甘德选择投降，我认为这具有双重意义。

sentences.en: As you say, he represents the English church, but also he's a figure who has every reason to try and continue the fight.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他代表了英格兰教会，但他也是一个完全有理由继续战斗的人。

sentences.en: And he hasn't.
sentences.zh: 但他没有。

sentences.en: He's basically kind of given in.
sentences.zh: 他基本上算是屈服了。

sentences.en: Edgar, though, still no sign of him.
sentences.zh: 不过，埃德加依然不见踪影。

sentences.en: And so William continues with his ravaging.
sentences.zh: 于是威廉继续他的劫掠。

sentences.en: And from Wallingford, he now turns back eastwards towards London, kind of closing in on the city from the north.
sentences.zh: 从沃灵福德出发，他现在转向东面，朝伦敦进发，从北面围困这座城市。

sentences.en: And the news of what is happening, of course, you know, reaches London.
sentences.zh: 当然，发生的事情的消息传到了伦敦。

sentences.en: Everyone is thrown into a state of absolute terror.
sentences.zh: 每个人都陷入了绝对的恐惧之中。

sentences.en: You've got refugees fleeing the advance of the Norman Knights.
sentences.zh: 难民们逃离诺曼骑士的推进。

sentences.en: They are bringing tales of all the horrors that are being inflicted by the invaders.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了入侵者所造成的种种恐怖故事。

sentences.en: People, you know, beg Edwin and Morka to march and defend them.
sentences.zh: 人们，你知道，恳求埃德温和莫卡出兵保卫他们。

sentences.en: They refuse and clearly the whole situation is hopeless.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝了，显然整个局势已经无可救药。

sentences.en: And Edgar essentially realises he has no prospect of holding out.
sentences.zh: 埃德加基本上意识到他没有任何坚持下去的希望。

sentences.en: And so he, Aildred, the Archbishop of York, Edwin, Morka, they all congregate and they go in procession to Berkhamstead in Hertfordshire, where William's army has camped.
sentences.zh: 于是他、约克大主教艾尔德雷德、埃德温、莫卡，他们聚集在一起，列队前往赫特福德郡的伯克汉姆斯特德，威廉的军队就在那里扎营。

sentences.en: But there isn't a burr there.
sentences.zh: 但那里并没有堡垒。

sentences.en: And so they're busy building a mot, a great mound of earth on which they will build a bailey, a fort.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正忙着建造一个土丘，一个巨大的土堆，他们将在上面建造一个外堡，一个要塞。

sentences.en: You can still see it to this day.
sentences.zh: 你至今仍能看到它。

sentences.en: And in fact, Jeff, my fishing coach, lives there and he's very proud of the of the mot and bailey there.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的钓鱼教练杰夫就住在那里，他为那里的土丘和外堡感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: So good to get Jeff in.
sentences.zh: 能提到杰夫真是太好了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so Edgar Atheling and all the chief men of London, Edwin and Morka, the Archbishop of York, they all come to William at Berkhamstead.
sentences.zh: 总之，埃德加·艾瑟林和伦敦的所有首领、埃德温和莫卡、约克大主教，他们都来到伯克汉姆斯特德见威廉。

sentences.en: And the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle describes their submission in tones of naked contempt.

sentences.en: So here's the thing.

sentences.zh: 他们从未遇到过有能力建造城堡的装甲骑兵。

sentences.zh: 当然，这正是哈罗德一直担心的。

sentences.zh: 但哈罗德明白英格兰人面临的是什么。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a kind of war of the world situation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种《世界大战》的情况。

sentences.en: Terrifying invaders burning all around.

sentences.en: So you can see why they would submit.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出他们为什么要投降。

sentences.en: And of course, with the submission of London and of Edgar Atheling, we come to the climax of 1066, of this most fateful of years.
sentences.zh: 当然，随着伦敦和埃德加·艾瑟林的投降，我们迎来了1066年的高潮，这是最决定性的一年。

sentences.en: William has achieved what he set out to achieve.
sentences.zh: 威廉实现了他想要实现的目标。

sentences.en: He has secured the heart of the kingdom before winter sets in very badly.
sentences.zh: 他在冬天变得非常糟糕之前稳固了王国的核心。

sentences.en: And by the time it is Christmas, so Christmas was the day that Charlemagne, of course, had been crowned.
sentences.zh: 到圣诞节的时候，当然，圣诞节是查理曼大帝加冕的日子，

sentences.zh: 威廉已经准备好自己加冕了。

sentences.zh: 所以他在圣诞节前几天进入了伦敦。

sentences.en: There is a massive military presence.
sentences.zh: 这里有大量的军队驻扎。

sentences.zh: 伦敦没有任何人会怀疑，他们正生活在一座被占领的城市里。

sentences.en: And immediately and inevitably, William orders the construction of a castle on the southeast corner of the city walls by the Thames.
sentences.zh: 威廉随即不可避免地下令，在泰晤士河畔的城墙东南角建造一座城堡。

sentences.en: And this castle is the castle that today we know is the Tower of London.
sentences.zh: 而这座城堡，就是我们今天所知的伦敦塔。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But of course, it's not only London itself behind its Roman walls that has fallen into his hands, so too has the great palace complex built by Edward the Confessor to the west of
sentences.zh: 当然，落入他手中的不仅是罗马城墙内的伦敦，还有忏悔者爱德华在伦敦西部建造的宏伟宫殿群。

sentences.en: London.
sentences.zh: 伦敦。

sentences.en: And it's not just a palace, it's a minster or an abbey.
sentences.zh: 那不仅仅是一座宫殿，更是一座大教堂或修道院。

sentences.en: So Westminster.
sentences.zh: 也就是威斯敏斯特。

sentences.en: And it is in Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day that William is crowned almost a year since
sentences.zh: 就在圣诞节那天，威廉在威斯敏斯特教堂加冕，距离哈罗德推测在那里加冕的时间已经过去近一年了。

sentences.en: Harold had presumably been crowned there.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德推测在那里加冕。

sentences.en: And everything seems utterly changed.
sentences.zh: 一切似乎都彻底改变了。

sentences.en: So outside the abbey, as William is being crowned, you have ranks of mailed French-speaking foreigners standing guard over the coronation of a king of England.
sentences.zh: 所以，当威廉在教堂外加冕时，一排排身披铠甲、说法语的外国人正守卫着这位英格兰国王的加冕礼。

sentences.en: Inside the abbey, you have another French innovation, the Archbishop of York and then a Norman bishop both step forward and ask the congregation if they will accept William as
sentences.zh: 在教堂内，还有另一项法国式的创新：约克大主教和一位诺曼主教先后走上前，询问会众是否愿意接受威廉为王。

sentences.en: king.
sentences.zh: 国王。

sentences.en: Aildred, the Archbishop of York in English, of course, but the French bishop in French.
sentences.zh: 约克大主教艾尔德雷德用英语询问，而那位法国主教则用法语。

sentences.en: And there is a great answering acclamation from the congregation in the abbey.
sentences.zh: 教堂里的会众发出了巨大的欢呼声作为回应。

sentences.en: And outside the abbey, this results, it is reported in chaos.
sentences.zh: 据报道，教堂外因此陷入了一片混乱。

sentences.en: William of Poitiers claims that the guards who are standing outside the abbey interpret the acclamation as English treachery.
sentences.zh: 普瓦捷的威廉声称，守在教堂外的卫兵将这欢呼声误解为英国人的背叛。

sentences.en: I mean, it's equally possible, in fact, probable that they've already, they're just going on the rampage, that they've just begun attacking people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，同样可能，甚至更有可能的是，他们当时已经开始横冲直撞，开始攻击民众了。

sentences.en: And certainly, whatever the reason for it, there is looting and there is burning of houses around
sentences.zh: 当然，无论原因是什么，威斯敏斯特教堂周围确实发生了抢劫和焚烧房屋的事件。

sentences.en: Westminster Abbey.
sentences.zh: 威斯敏斯特教堂。

sentences.en: An incredibly ominous and dramatic scene.
sentences.zh: 一个极其不祥且戏剧性的场景。

sentences.en: Very ominous.
sentences.zh: 非常不祥。

sentences.en: And members of the congregation hurry out to help fight the flames.
sentences.zh: 会众中的成员匆忙跑出去帮忙扑灭大火。

sentences.en: And Audric Fatalis, who is this Anglo-Norman, identifies as English, writing in Normandy,
sentences.zh: 奥德里克·维塔利斯，这位在诺曼底写作、自认为是英国人的盎格鲁-诺曼人，

sentences.en: he says of this, that only the bishops and clergy, along with the monks, stayed terrified in front of the altar.
sentences.zh: 他在描述此事时说，只有主教、神职人员和僧侣们惊恐地留在祭坛前。

sentences.en: But the service still goes ahead and William is anointed, crowned, and then he sits on his
sentences.zh: 但仪式仍在继续，威廉接受了涂油礼和加冕，随后坐上了他的宝座，

sentences.en: throne, even though the pews are pretty much empty and there are screams and the crackling of flames coming from outside the abbey doors.
sentences.zh: 尽管长椅几乎空无一人，教堂门外还传来尖叫声和火焰燃烧的噼啪声。

sentences.en: But he could sit there and think, well, you know, my gamble, the odds were so immense.
sentences.zh: 但他可以坐在那里心想，好吧，你知道，我的赌注，胜算曾经是如此渺茫。

sentences.en: But his gamble has succeeded.
sentences.zh: 但他的赌博成功了。

sentences.en: He's no longer a duke.
sentences.zh: 他不再是一位公爵。

sentences.en: He is now an anointed king.
sentences.zh: 他现在是一位受膏的国王。

sentences.en: And when his followers salute him, as they do, now that he's been crowned, they do so in terms that place him on a level, basically with only two other rulers in Latin Christendom.
sentences.zh: 当他的追随者向他致敬时——正如他们在他加冕后所做的那样——他们所用的称谓，基本上将他与拉丁基督教世界中仅有的另外两位统治者置于同一水平。

sentences.en: And that is the emperor and the king of France.
sentences.zh: 那就是皇帝和法国国王。

sentences.en: So this man has gone from being a duke to being an anointed king, whose followers hail him in
sentences.zh: 所以这个男人从一位公爵变成了一位受膏的国王，他的追随者们用这些称谓来赞美他：

sentences.en: these terms, to the most serene William, the great and peace-giving king, crowned by God, life and victory.
sentences.zh: 致最尊贵的威廉，伟大而带来和平的国王，上帝加冕者，生命与胜利。

sentences.en: So for William to be hailed in this way, I mean, it is the ultimate fruit of conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，威廉能以这种方式受到欢呼，我的意思是，这是征服的终极果实。

sentences.en: And yet the weird thing is, so we talked about whether Hastings finishes Anglo-Saxon England off for good.
sentences.zh: 然而奇怪的是，我们之前讨论过黑斯廷斯战役是否彻底终结了盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰。

sentences.en: The weird thing is, is that William's coronation in Westminster Abbey is actually a symbol of continuity as well as of rupture.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，威廉在威斯敏斯特教堂的加冕礼，实际上既是断裂的象征，也是连续的象征。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。

sentences.en: Well, let's see what William is thinking.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们看看威廉在想什么。

sentences.en: So Audric Vitalis tells us that as he's being consecrated, so as he's being anointed, he trembled violently.
sentences.zh: 奥德里克·维塔利斯告诉我们，当他接受祝圣，也就是接受涂油礼时，他剧烈地颤抖着。

sentences.en: And people have often wondered, you know, why?
sentences.zh: 人们经常会问，你知道，为什么？

sentences.zh: 很多人认为，也许他是在反思自己为了夺取王位所做的一切，你知道。

sentences.en: He knows he's going to help.
sentences.zh: 他知道他会得到帮助。

sentences.en: And maybe the flickering of flames outside the doors of the Abbey only enhance that.
sentences.zh: 也许教堂门外闪烁的火焰只会加剧这种感觉。

sentences.en: But I think it's unlikely.
sentences.zh: 但我认为不太可能。

sentences.en: I don't think William is the kind of person to have doubts at the climactic moment of his triumph, because I think it's much more likely that he is feeling awe before the God-given
sentences.zh: 我不认为威廉是那种会在胜利的关键时刻产生怀疑的人，因为我觉得更有可能的是，他感受到了上帝赋予他的责任的敬畏，这些责任是上帝在重重困难中托付给他的。

sentences.en: scale of his responsibilities that God has entrusted into his hands against all the odds.
sentences.zh: 规模的责任，上帝在重重困难中托付给他的。

sentences.en: So he is a conqueror.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一位征服者。

sentences.en: He will come to be known as the conqueror, but he's not being crowned as a conqueror.
sentences.zh: 他最终会被称为“征服者”，但他加冕时并非以征服者的身份。

sentences.en: I think that the sense in which, in William's own opinion, he is being crowned as the heir of
sentences.zh: 我认为，在威廉自己看来，他作为忏悔者爱德华继承人的身份被掩盖了，因为加冕礼的一切都在宣示：他加冕并非凭借他用剑赢得的胜利，而是凭借权利。

sentences.en: Edward the Confessor tends to be obscured, because everything about that coronation is proclaiming that he is being crowned not by virtue of the victories he's won with his
sentences.zh: 爱德华的继承人，往往被掩盖了，因为加冕礼的一切都在宣示，他加冕并非凭借他用剑赢得的胜利，

sentences.en: sword, but by right.
sentences.zh: 而是凭借权利。

sentences.en: That he is the legitimate heir, not just to Edward the Confessor, but to the line of kings that stretches back to Alfred all the way to Kurdic.
sentences.zh: 他是合法的继承人，不仅是忏悔者爱德华的继承人，也是从阿尔弗雷德一直追溯到塞尔迪克的国王世系的继承人。

sentences.en: That he is truly the anointed king of England.
sentences.zh: 他是真正的英格兰受膏国王。

sentences.en: So it's being held in Westminster Abbey, built by Edward the Confessor.
sentences.zh: 所以加冕礼在忏悔者爱德华建造的威斯敏斯特教堂举行。

sentences.en: The coronation ritual, although there are a few interpolations that come from French practice,
sentences.zh: 加冕仪式虽然加入了一些源自法国习俗的插曲，

sentences.en: in the main, it's exactly the consecration rite that had been staged at Bath when Edgar had been crowned, right back at the beginning of our story.
sentences.zh: 但总体上，它正是我们故事开头埃德加在巴斯加冕时所采用的祝圣仪式，没错吧？

sentences.en: And he is consecrated as the ruler of the Anglo-Saxonarchy, the Anglo-Saxons.
sentences.zh: 他被祝圣为盎格鲁-撒克逊政权的统治者，盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王。

sentences.en: And this is a formula that goes back to Alfred.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可以追溯到阿尔弗雷德时代的公式。

sentences.en: So he is being crowned as king of the Anglo-Saxons, of England.
sentences.zh: 所以他被加冕为盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王，英格兰的国王。

sentences.en: Just to be clear, they absolutely use the term Anglo-Saxons.
sentences.zh: 明确一点，他们绝对使用了“盎格鲁-撒克逊人”这个词。

sentences.en: So if there's any very excitable American academics listening, listen to those words and reflect on your behaviour.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有任何激动的美国学者在听，请听听这些词，反思一下你们的行为。

sentences.en: And I think you're right to fix on that.
sentences.zh: 我想你关注这一点是对的。

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't gel with our sense of what the Norman Conquest is about, that William is being crowned as king of the Anglo-Saxons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，威廉被加冕为盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王，这与我们对诺曼征服的理解并不吻合。

sentences.en: And that's because, of course, 1066 is probably the profoundest rupture in English history.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是因为1066年可能是英国历史上最深刻的断裂。

sentences.en: It's a year of invasion, of bloodshed, absolutely, of conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 那是一年充满了入侵、流血，绝对是征服的一年。

sentences.en: But it is also a year which ends with this very public, very ringing insistence that there is continuity as well as rupture.
sentences.zh: 但这一年也以这种非常公开、非常响亮的坚持而告终：既有连续性，也有断裂。

sentences.en: And even though it's obvious that William's rule depends on mailed force, you know, that's what all those soldiers are doing outside the abbey, it does also depend on him showing
sentences.zh: 尽管威廉的统治显然依赖于武装力量——你知道，教堂外那些士兵所做的就是这些——但它也依赖于他对他新王国的历史和传统的尊重。

sentences.en: I think the evidence makes it pretty clear that William was not what he did not want to eliminate the English aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 我认为证据很清楚地表明，威廉并不想消灭英国贵族。

sentences.en: I mean, clearly he had to reward his followers with lands and the death of the Godwinsons gave him perfect opportunity to do that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然他必须用土地奖励他的追随者，而戈德温家族的覆灭给了他绝佳的机会。

sentences.en: But he was hoping that the English aristocracy would collaborate with him.
sentences.zh: 但他原本是希望英国贵族能与他合作的。

sentences.en: But instead, they just keep rising in insurrection after insurrection.
sentences.zh: 但相反，他们不断地发动起义。

sentences.en: And so year after year, there are these bushfires of rebellion across England.
sentences.zh: 所以年复一年，英格兰各地到处都是叛乱的火苗。

sentences.en: And year after year, brutal man that he is, William stamps them out.
sentences.zh: 而年复一年，作为残暴之人的威廉，将它们一一扑灭。

sentences.en: And it's not just the native aristocracy who suffer terribly from this process.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个过程中，遭受惨重损失的不仅仅是本土贵族。

sentences.en: So lots of the of the peasantry in England suffer as well.
sentences.zh: 英格兰的许多农民也深受其害。

sentences.en: And the most notorious example of this is a series of campaigns that were waged in Northumbria, southern Northumbria in the winter of 1069 to 70,
sentences.zh: 最臭名昭著的例子是1069年冬至1070年间在诺森布里亚南部进行的一系列战役，

sentences.en: which is remembered as the harrying of the north.
sentences.zh: 也就是人们记忆中的“哈罗英格兰北部”事件。

sentences.en: Very, very notorious kind of mass destruction, mass looting, the deliberate targeting of food supplies.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常臭名昭著的大规模破坏、大规模掠夺，以及蓄意针对粮食供应的打击。

sentences.en: So that over the course of the winter, maybe 150,000 people may have died of starvation, 80,000 oxen.
sentences.zh: 那个冬天，可能有15万人死于饥饿，还有8万头牛。

sentences.en: These are the kind of the likely figures.
sentences.zh: 这些是大概的数字。

sentences.en: And even William's admirers were shocked.
sentences.zh: 即使是威廉的崇拜者也感到震惊。

sentences.en: So to quote Aldrich Vitalis, famous, famous passage, he wrote,
sentences.zh: 引用奥尔德里克·维塔利斯那段非常著名的段落，他写道：

sentences.en: My narrative has frequently had occasion to praise William, but for this act, which condemned the innocent and guilty alike to die by slow starvation, I cannot commend him.
sentences.zh: “我的叙述经常有机会赞美威廉，但对于这一行为，它使无辜者和有罪者同样死于缓慢的饥饿，我无法称赞他。”

sentences.en: For when I think of helpless children, young men in the prime of life and hoary gray beards perishing alike of hunger,
sentences.zh: “因为当我想到无助的孩子、正值壮年的年轻人和白发苍苍的老人同样死于饥饿时，

sentences.en: I am so moved to pity that I would rather lament the grief and sufferings of the wretched people than make a vain attempt to flatter the perpetrator of such infamy.
sentences.zh: 我感到无比怜悯，我宁愿哀悼这些可怜人的悲伤和苦难，也不愿徒劳地去奉承这种暴行的始作俑者。”

sentences.en: So that's punchy stuff.
sentences.zh: 这话说得很有力。

sentences.en: It is punchy.
sentences.zh: 确实很有力。

sentences.en: And it's not my normal thing to sort of defend William, but I'm reminded of the thing we talked about with Harald Hardrada in Norway.
sentences.zh: 虽然为威廉辩护不是我的常态，但我回想起我们谈论挪威的哈拉尔·哈德拉达时提到的事情。

sentences.en: You remember when he was chastising the farmers of the uplands who had not paid their taxes?
sentences.zh: 你还记得他惩罚那些没有缴纳税款的高地农民吗？

sentences.en: And maybe you could argue this is simply what a ruthless 11th century king does when he's, you know, it's part of the assertion of royal authority.
sentences.zh: 也许你可以说，这就是一个冷酷的11世纪国王在维护王权时所做的事情。

sentences.en: You know, when you've got the emergence of stronger and stronger kingdoms and you've got kings who are serious people, as Harald Hardrada and William the Conqueror clearly were.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当出现越来越强大的王国，并且有像哈拉尔·哈德拉达和威廉征服者这样严肃的国王时，

sentences.en: And, you know, you step out of line and they will, I mean, they will kill you.
sentences.zh: 如果你不守规矩，他们就会杀了你。

sentences.en: Well, the other thing, and this again is a contrast with Harald Hardrada or indeed with Canute, is that the harrying of entire populations,
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有一点，这与哈拉尔·哈德拉达甚至克努特大帝形成了对比，那就是对整个族群的蹂躏，

sentences.en: which Harald Hardrada absolutely had done, is not the only thing that William can do to secure his rule over England.
sentences.zh: 虽然哈拉尔·哈德拉达确实做过，但这并不是威廉巩固其对英格兰统治的唯一手段。

sentences.en: Because, of course, William comes as the representative of this new military culture that is hugely investing in the construction of castles.
sentences.zh: 因为威廉带来的这种新的军事文化，在城堡建设上投入了巨大精力。

sentences.en: So, again, let's go back to imagining that we're travelling with the Norman landowners to this great assembly convened by William in Salisbury on the 1st of August, 1086.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们回到想象中，我们正与诺曼土地所有者一起前往1086年8月1日威廉在索尔兹伯里召集的盛大集会。

sentences.en: And what would we see ahead of us?
sentences.zh: 我们前方会看到什么？

sentences.en: So we are not, those who know Salisbury, now the town is down by the water meadows where the great cathedral with its tall spire stands.
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到的不是索尔兹伯里，现在的城镇位于水草丰美的草地上，那里矗立着拥有高耸尖顶的大教堂。

sentences.en: There's nothing there at this point.
sentences.zh: 那时那里什么都没有。

sentences.en: Salisbury is a great Iron Age hill fort at the place that is now known as Old Serum.
sentences.zh: 索尔兹伯里是一座巨大的铁器时代山堡，位于现在被称为老萨勒姆的地方。

sentences.en: And it had been re-fortified by Aethelred and he'd set a mint up there.
sentences.zh: 它曾被埃塞尔雷德重新加固，他还在那里设立了一个造币厂。

sentences.en: So it was a fortified point for the Anglo-Saxon kings.
sentences.zh: 所以它是盎格鲁-撒克逊国王的一个防御点。

sentences.en: But William has inevitably made it even more impregnable.
sentences.zh: 但威廉不可避免地使它变得更加坚不可摧。

sentences.en: He's built a massive modern bailey right in the centre of Old Serum and it is ruled directly by the king.
sentences.zh: 他在老萨勒姆的中心建造了一个巨大的现代外庭，并由国王直接统治。

sentences.en: So we've mentioned the Norman landowners, but by far the largest landowner is William himself.
sentences.zh: 我们提到了诺曼土地所有者，但到目前为止，最大的土地所有者是威廉本人。

sentences.en: So huge, huge direct control over vast arrays of estates and of fortifications.
sentences.zh: 他对大量的庄园和防御工事拥有巨大的直接控制权。

sentences.en: And Salisbury is one of them.
sentences.zh: 索尔兹伯里就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Windsor is another.
sentences.zh: 温莎是另一个。

sentences.en: The Tower of London, another.
sentences.zh: 伦敦塔是又一个。

sentences.en: Still royal fortresses to this day.
sentences.zh: 直到今天它们仍然是皇家堡垒。

sentences.en: But William, of course, is not the only castle builder.
sentences.zh: 但威廉当然不是唯一的城堡建造者。

sentences.en: Pretty much every Norman landowner is building them.
sentences.zh: 几乎每个诺曼土地所有者都在建造城堡。

sentences.en: And of course they're doing this because they're a tiny minority surrounded by exceedingly hostile natives.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们这样做是因为他们是被极其敌视的当地人包围的极少数群体。

sentences.en: And the fact that they are able to protect themselves in these fortifications, I mean, that sets them apart from, say,
sentences.zh: 他们能够利用这些防御工事保护自己，这使他们区别于，比如说，

sentences.en: the Viking warlords who had done this before and who very rapidly had kind of merged into the mass of the English who surround them.
sentences.zh: 那些以前这样做过，并很快融入周围英国人大众中的维京军阀。

sentences.en: This is not the case with these Norman landowners.
sentences.zh: 这些诺曼土地所有者的情况并非如此。

sentences.en: They are very obviously physically separate from the people they're ruling because they're surrounded by, you know, these ramparts.
sentences.zh: 他们显然在物理上与他们统治的人民隔离开来，因为他们被这些城墙包围着。

sentences.en: And this is recognised by the English themselves straight away.
sentences.zh: 这一点英国人自己也立刻意识到了。

sentences.en: So the entry for 1066 in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, it recorded how Norman warlords built castles far and wide throughout this country and distressed the wretched folk.
sentences.zh: 《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》中1066年的条目记录了诺曼军阀如何在全国各地建造城堡，并使可怜的民众陷入困境。

sentences.en: And always after that, it grew much worse.
sentences.zh: 此后情况变得越来越糟。

sentences.en: May the end be good when God wills.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑，结局能是好的。

sentences.en: But here's a thing.
sentences.zh: 但有一件事。

sentences.en: So visitors to a major English town and what would have been a major medieval town, if they go today, there are actually two structures that will often dominate the town.
sentences.zh: 如果今天有人去参观一个主要的英国城镇，也就是曾经的主要中世纪城镇，通常会有两个结构主导着城镇。

sentences.en: So one will be the castle or the ruins of the castle.
sentences.zh: 一个是城堡或城堡的废墟。

sentences.en: But the other is often obviously the cathedral or a big church.
sentences.zh: 但另一个显然通常是大教堂或大教堂。

sentences.en: And that's the other side of this, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是另一面，不是吗？

sentences.en: So it's partly military power, but it's also, as you've described so often, a kind of spiritual power.
sentences.zh: 所以这部分是军事力量，但正如你经常描述的那样，这也是一种精神力量。

sentences.en: So there's a religious dimension to this conquest as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这场征服也有宗教层面。

sentences.en: There is.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: And so, again, if you're coming up to Old Sarum, you're coming up to Salisbury, you'd see the castle.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你再次来到老萨勒姆，来到索尔兹伯里，你会看到城堡。

sentences.en: But you would also see a half-completed cathedral, which is massive.
sentences.zh: 但你也会看到一座尚未完工的巨大大教堂。

sentences.en: Workmen have been toiling away for pretty much a decade.
sentences.zh: 工人们已经辛苦劳作了近十年。

sentences.en: And as you say, it's part of a huge programme of church building in England that is, I mean, completely unprecedented in the scale of its ambition.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这是英格兰大规模教堂建设规划的一部分，其雄心壮志是前所未有的。

sentences.en: And most of the medieval cathedrals that still dominate English cathedral towns to this day were almost all of them either founded or actually constructed in the main in the immediate wake of the conquest or,
sentences.zh: 今天仍然主导着英国大教堂城镇的大多数中世纪大教堂，几乎都是在征服后立即建立或建造的，或者，

sentences.en: you know, a generation or so after it.
sentences.zh: 是在那之后的一代人左右。

sentences.en: And of the Anglo-Saxon minsters, I mean, barely a brick of those was left standing.
sentences.zh: 至于盎格鲁-撒克逊人的修道院，几乎连一块砖都没剩下。

sentences.en: And the Norman cathedrals that were built on the site of the Anglo-Saxon cathedrals, I mean, they don't just obliterate the memory of the Anglo-Saxon church,
sentences.zh: 而在盎格鲁-撒克逊大教堂遗址上建造的诺曼大教堂，不仅抹去了盎格鲁-撒克逊教会的记忆，

sentences.en: but they establish an imprint on the country that was designed to laSt.
sentences.zh: 而且在全国留下了旨在长存的印记。

sentences.en: And in fact, the cathedral that's being built on Old Sarum, I mean,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在老萨勒姆建造的大教堂，

sentences.en: it's one of the very few examples of a cathedral over the course of the Middle Ages that gets replaced in its entirety,
sentences.zh: 是中世纪极少数被完全拆除重建的大教堂之一，

sentences.en: because ultimately people decide that Old Sarum is too inconvenient.
sentences.zh: 因为人们最终认为老萨勒姆太不方便了。

sentences.en: And so they move down to the lowlands below Old Sarum, which is where Salisbury Cathedral, as it stands today, is then kind of rebuilt.
sentences.zh: 于是他们搬到了老萨勒姆下方的低地，也就是今天索尔兹伯里大教堂重建的地方。

sentences.en: So this programme of church building is the kind of the physical expression, as you said, of a kind of great revolution in the affairs of the English church more broadly.
sentences.zh: 所以这个教堂建设规划，正如你所说，是英国教会事务中一场大革命的物理表现。

sentences.en: And so just as the aristocracy, the English aristocracy has been eliminated, so too have English bishops been removed from the commanding heights of the church.
sentences.zh: 正如英国贵族被消灭一样，英国主教也被从教会的指挥高层中清除出去了。

sentences.en: And in fact, by 1086, you have only a single English bishop still in office.
sentences.zh: 事实上，到1086年，只剩下一位英国主教还在任。

sentences.en: And the justification for this is the sense that the English church had been very, very sick and corrupt.
sentences.zh: 其理由是认为英国教会已经病入膏肓且腐败不堪。

sentences.en: So the fact that Stiggan, the Archbishop of Canterbury, had surrendered to William doesn't stop him from being deposed in 1070.
sentences.zh: 所以，坎特伯雷大主教斯蒂甘向威廉投降的事实，并没有阻止他在1070年被罢免。

sentences.en: And he gets replaced by this Italian monk who had been talent spotted by William and recruited to serve him in Normandy as the abbot of an abbey in Caen.
sentences.zh: 他被一位意大利僧侣取代，该僧侣被威廉看中，并被招募到诺曼底担任卡昂一座修道院的院长。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Lanfranc.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫兰弗兰克。

sentences.en: And if Stiggan had been a byword for corruption, Lanfranc is the greatest theologian of his day.
sentences.zh: 如果说斯蒂甘是腐败的代名词，那么兰弗兰克就是他那个时代最伟大的神学家。

sentences.en: I mean, an incredibly impressive figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一个令人印象深刻的人物。

sentences.en: And he is the embodiment of everything that is most radical, most innovative, most kind of spiritually impressive, to be honest,
sentences.zh: 老实说，他体现了最激进、最创新、在精神层面最令人印象深刻的一切，

sentences.en: about this kind of process of reformation that is associated with Gregory VII, the extraordinary pope, and this kind of reform movement,
sentences.zh: 关于这种与非凡的教皇格列高利七世相关的改革进程，以及这种改革运动，

sentences.en: and which the English, now that they've been defeated, have no choice but to submit to.
sentences.zh: 而英国人既然已经被击败，也就别无选择，只能屈服于此。

sentences.en: And I think because they are demoralized, and every time we quote an English chronicler commenting on their defeat, they all say, you know, this is because of our sins.
sentences.zh: 我认为是因为他们士气低落，每当我们引用英国编年史作者对他们战败的评论时，他们都会说，你知道，这是因为我们的罪孽。

sentences.en: This is what God wants.
sentences.zh: 这就是上帝想要的。

sentences.en: We are being punished for our sins.
sentences.zh: 我们正在为我们的罪孽受罚。

sentences.en: And so I think for that reason, they are prepared to accept the fact that clearly their church was not pleasing to God.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为出于这个原因，他们准备接受这样一个事实，即他们的教会显然并没有取悦上帝。

sentences.en: And therefore, perhaps, you know, the Aegean stable has to be cleansed.
sentences.zh: 因此，也许，你知道，奥革阿斯的牛圈必须被清理干净。

sentences.en: So that is also part of the great revolution that the Normans have brought.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是诺曼人带来的伟大革命的一部分。

sentences.en: And that castle, that half-completed cathedral, they are absolutely symbols of the rupture that the conquest has precipitated.
sentences.zh: 那座城堡，那座未完工的大教堂，绝对是征服所引发的断裂的象征。

sentences.en: And a further evidence for the scale of the rupture is there in the reason that these landowners have been summoned to Salisbury on Lammas,
sentences.zh: 而这种断裂规模的进一步证据，在于这些土地所有者在拉马斯节被传唤到索尔兹伯里的原因，

sentences.en: so the first harvest of the year, so the 1st of August, 1086.
sentences.zh: 也就是一年中的第一次收获，即1086年8月1日。

sentences.en: So we're told by the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, why were they gathered there?
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史告诉我们，他们为什么要聚集在那里？

sentences.en: To submit to him and swear oaths of allegiance to him that they would be faithful to him against all other men.
sentences.zh: 为了向他臣服并宣誓效忠，承诺在对抗所有其他人时对他保持忠诚。

sentences.en: So this is, again, a consolidation of William's power as king that is radical and revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 所以这再次巩固了威廉作为国王的权力，这是激进且革命性的。

sentences.en: The Anglo-Saxon king, we've talked about this, did not hold all of the land of England.
sentences.zh: 我们谈过，盎格鲁-撒克逊国王并没有拥有英格兰所有的土地。

sentences.en: But effectively, this is what William is instituting.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这正是威廉正在建立的制度。

sentences.en: Because with this oath, every landowner in England is now accepting publicly that he holds his land directly from William.
sentences.zh: 因为有了这个誓言，英格兰的每一位土地所有者现在都在公开承认，他直接从威廉手中持有土地。

sentences.en: Tom, I fear that we're teetering on the brink of a discussion of the feudal system, which would be a terrifying prospect.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我担心我们正处于讨论封建制度的边缘，那将是一个可怕的前景。

sentences.en: It would.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So let's not use abstract nouns.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不要使用抽象名词。

sentences.en: I mean, you'll find it unusual for me to say that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你会觉得我这么说很反常。

sentences.en: Let's just look at what it means in practical terms for these landowners who are coming and swearing this oath.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看对于这些前来宣誓的土地所有者来说，这在实际层面上意味着什么。

sentences.en: So what it does is these landowners have gone through enormous turbulence.
sentences.zh: 它所做的是，这些土地所有者经历了巨大的动荡。

sentences.en: You've had rebellions.
sentences.zh: 你们经历了叛乱。

sentences.en: You've had the native aristocracy kind of rising up, being eliminated, being forced into exile, whatever.
sentences.zh: 你们经历了本土贵族起义、被消灭、被迫流亡等等。

sentences.en: And so the legal documents that might enable these new Norman landowners to feel secure in their possessions are not really there.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些能让这些新诺曼土地所有者对自己的财产感到安全的法律文件并不真正存在。

sentences.en: And so this is what William has been trying to rectify.
sentences.zh: 这就是威廉一直试图纠正的事情。

sentences.en: And for seven months, his agents have been going around England and recording who owns what land.
sentences.zh: 七个月来，他的代理人一直在英格兰各地记录谁拥有什么土地。

sentences.en: And these agents are recording two key details.
sentences.zh: 这些代理人记录了两个关键细节。

sentences.en: So they're recording who owned the land when Edward the Confessor died on the 5th of January 1066.
sentences.zh: 他们记录了1066年1月5日忏悔者爱德华去世时，谁拥有这些土地。

sentences.en: And who are the landowners now?
sentences.zh: 以及现在的土地所有者是谁？

sentences.en: And observant listeners will note that that completely eliminates Harold.
sentences.zh: 细心的听众会注意到，这完全排除了哈罗德。

sentences.en: So Harold has been erased from the historical record.
sentences.zh: 所以哈罗德已经被从历史记录中抹去了。

sentences.en: And these records, after this great meeting at Salisbury, will be copied out by a single scribe and come to be known in due course as Doomsday Book.
sentences.zh: 在索尔兹伯里的这次大会之后，这些记录将由一名抄写员抄写，并最终被称为《末日审判书》。

sentences.en: And it's likely that that name is being applied to it very, very early on.
sentences.zh: 而且很可能这个名字在很早的时候就被应用了。

sentences.en: And it is called Doomsday Book because the presumption is that what has been recorded is unalterable,
sentences.zh: 它被称为《末日审判书》，因为人们认为所记录的内容是不可更改的，

sentences.en: like the judgments that will be delivered at the end of days, you know, the day of judgment.
sentences.zh: 就像世界末日时将作出的判决一样，你知道，审判日。

sentences.en: And what the Doomsday Book stands for is the recognition that there's an entirely new order, right?
sentences.zh: 《末日审判书》所代表的是对一个全新秩序的认可，对吧？

sentences.en: That there's been a massive transfer of property and power from one social group to another, from the English aristocracy to the Norman aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 即发生了从一个社会群体到另一个社会群体的巨大财产和权力转移，从英国贵族到诺曼贵族。

sentences.en: And the point is that like the cathedrals and the castles, this is going to last forever.
sentences.zh: 重点是，就像大教堂和城堡一样，这将永远持续下去。

sentences.en: There's no turning back now.
sentences.zh: 现在已经没有回头路了。

sentences.en: That was 20 years ago and it's set in stone, literally, in the case of the castles and the cathedrals.
sentences.zh: 那是20年前的事了，而且已经刻在石头上了，在城堡和大教堂的情况下，确实如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And everybody accepts that.
sentences.zh: 每个人都接受这一点。

sentences.en: Do you think by this point?
sentences.zh: 你认为到了这个时候吗？

sentences.en: So, I mean, there may be a few people who, in their cups late at night, look back to the old days.
sentences.zh: 我是说，可能有一些人在深夜喝醉时，会回顾过去的日子。

sentences.en: But by and large, everyone accepts the world has changed.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，每个人都接受世界已经改变了。

sentences.en: Yes, maybe.
sentences.zh: 是的，也许吧。

sentences.en: Although one of the things that has precipitated William's desire to compile this great legal record
sentences.zh: 尽管威廉渴望编制这份伟大的法律记录的原因之一，

sentences.en: is the fact that for about a year, William's hold on England has actually seemed quite precarious.
sentences.zh: 是因为大约一年来，威廉对英格兰的控制实际上看起来相当不稳定。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is one that you touched on in your account of Harold Hardrada, where you said, is he the last of the Vikings?
sentences.zh: 原因就是你在讲述哈拉尔·哈德拉达时提到的，你说，他是最后一个维京人吗？

sentences.en: Well, actually, no, he's not, because there are still Scandinavian kings who aspire to conquer England.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实不是，因为仍然有斯堪的纳维亚国王渴望征服英格兰。

sentences.en: And this is very evident in the circumstances that give birth to the Doomsday Book.
sentences.zh: 这一点在《末日审判书》诞生的背景中非常明显。

sentences.en: So what prompted it is the prospect of an invasion by the Danish king, Canute.
sentences.zh: 促成它的是丹麦国王克努特入侵的前景。

sentences.en: So this is the Canute, the nephew of the famous Canute, who'd been the great adversary of Harold Hardrada and is still very much on the scene
sentences.zh: 这就是那位著名的克努特的侄子，他曾是哈拉尔·哈德拉达的劲敌，而且仍然活跃在舞台上，

sentences.en: and is threatening to launch a full-born amphibious invasion of William's kingdom.
sentences.zh: 并威胁要对威廉的王国发动全面的两栖入侵。

sentences.en: And so William, very like Athelred, wants to know how much money he's got and where he can obtain it from.
sentences.zh: 所以威廉，非常像埃塞尔雷德，想知道他有多少钱，以及从哪里可以获得这些钱。

sentences.en: And he does this in the full consciousness that Scandinavian warlords are still on the scene.
sentences.zh: 他这样做时，完全意识到斯堪的纳维亚军阀仍然在场。

sentences.en: So in 1069, Svein, the Danish king, had sailed up the Humber and William had paid the Danes off, just as Athelred might have done.
sentences.zh: 所以在1069年，丹麦国王斯文航行上了亨伯河，威廉付钱打发了丹麦人，就像埃塞尔雷德可能做的那样。

sentences.en: And obviously, William is not Athelred.
sentences.zh: 显然，威廉不是埃塞尔雷德。

sentences.en: But again and again, throughout his reign, he is doing as Athelred had sought to do, which is essentially to exploit to the full
sentences.zh: 但他在整个统治期间一次又一次地做着埃塞尔雷德曾经试图做的事情，本质上就是充分利用

sentences.en: the incredible wealth and administrative know-how of his kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他王国惊人的财富和行政知识。

sentences.en: And so in that sense, the Doomsday Book, as well as being the final nail in the coffin
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，《末日审判书》不仅是盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰棺材上的最后一颗钉子，

sentences.en: of Anglo-Saxon England, as you said, kind of a public proclamation that everything has changed, is also the kind of the last hurrah of that Anglo-Saxon state.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这是一种公开宣告一切都已经改变，也是盎格鲁-撒克逊国家最后的绝唱。

sentences.en: And the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle writing about it, I mean, he expresses shock at how intrusive
sentences.zh: 而撰写它的《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》，表达了对威廉代理人目光是多么具有侵入性的震惊，

sentences.en: William's agent's eyes.
sentences.zh: 威廉代理人的眼睛。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So very narrowly did he have everywhere investigated that there was no single hide nor yard of land, nor indeed, it is a shame to relate, but it seemed no shame
sentences.zh: 他调查得如此细致，以至于没有一海德或一码土地，甚至，说出来都觉得羞耻，但对他来说似乎并不羞耻，

sentences.en: to him to do, one ox, nor one cow, nor one pig was there left out and not put down in his record.
sentences.zh: 一头牛，甚至一头猪，都没有被遗漏，没有被写进他的记录里。

sentences.en: But even as the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle is complaining about this, what it is recording is a measure of governmental sophistication that is only possible in a kingdom like England.
sentences.zh: 但即使《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》在抱怨这一点，它所记录的正是只有像英格兰这样的王国才可能有的政府复杂程度。

sentences.en: Doomsday Book could not have been compiled anywhere else in Latin Christendom, which is why it's so exceptional.
sentences.zh: 《末日审判书》不可能在拉丁基督教世界的任何其他地方编制出来，这就是它如此特别的原因。

sentences.en: And it marks William out, not just as someone who is a conqueror, but also as someone who is
sentences.zh: 它不仅将威廉标记为征服者，而且还将他标记为

sentences.en: exploiting the resources of his kingdom far more ably than Athelred, you know, or the Confessor had been able to do, you know.
sentences.zh: 比埃塞尔雷德或忏悔者更有效地利用王国资源的人。

sentences.en: And so in a sense, the strength of his monarchy is a reflection of the very kingdom that he's conquered.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，他君主制的强大正是他所征服的这个王国的反映。

sentences.en: And I think you could, I mean, you know, there are other examples as well where things that are notorious as markers of William's conquest of England, you can place it
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以，我是说，还有其他例子，那些作为威廉征服英格兰标志的臭名昭著的事情，你可以把它

sentences.en: in a line of descent from what Anglo-Saxon kings were doing.
sentences.zh: 放在盎格鲁-撒克逊国王所做之事的传承线上。

sentences.en: So the harrying of the North, for instance.
sentences.zh: 例如，对北方的蹂躏。

sentences.en: I mean, the most notorious episode of his reign as king, but he's behaving as Edgar had done.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他作为国王统治期间最臭名昭著的事件，但他表现得就像埃德加曾经做过的那样。

sentences.en: You know, we began this series with Edgar.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们以埃德加开始了这一系列。

sentences.en: Edgar the Peaceable.
sentences.zh: 和平者埃德加。

sentences.en: Edgar the Peaceable, the Pacificus.
sentences.zh: 和平者埃德加，太平洋主义者。

sentences.en: And Edgar is called Pacificus because he guaranteed order.
sentences.zh: 埃德加被称为和平者，因为他保证了秩序。

sentences.en: And William is called Pacificus.
sentences.zh: 而威廉被称为和平者。

sentences.en: You know, those anthems that get sung to him after his coronation, he's hailed as peacegiving, exactly as Edgar had been.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在他加冕后为他唱的那些赞美诗，他被誉为和平的给予者，正如埃德加一样。

sentences.en: And William is peacegiving because he also deals out death and destruction to those who rebel against him.
sentences.zh: 威廉是和平的给予者，因为他也对那些反抗他的人施加死亡和毁灭。

sentences.en: And that is very Anglo-Saxon.
sentences.zh: 这非常盎格鲁-撒克逊。

sentences.en: And yet, maybe we could push that too far because we do know, because it comes up in English
sentences.zh: 然而，也许我们不能走得太远，因为我们确实知道，因为它出现在英国

sentences.en: Chronicles and things, that the English, the native-born English, do have a profound sense of trauma that has passed down the generations because of this.
sentences.zh: 编年史等文献中，英国人，本土出生的英国人，确实有一种深刻的创伤感，因为这件事而代代相传。

sentences.en: So we could dress this up and say, oh, it's a lovely balancing act.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以粉饰一下，说，哦，这是一个可爱的平衡行为。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're working in the Anglo-Saxon state.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们在盎格鲁-撒克逊国家工作。

sentences.en: But this is a genuinely kind of traumatic and it's a massive rupture for, if you're living through this, you feel it as a huge rupture, don't you?
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一种创伤，对于经历这一切的人来说，这是一种巨大的断裂，你感觉到了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And William, I mean, he knows this as well as anybody.
sentences.zh: 威廉，我是说，他比任何人都清楚这一点。

sentences.en: I think it's pretty clear that William does suffer a slightly guilty conscience about it.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，威廉确实为此感到有些内疚。

sentences.en: So we've already mentioned how he pays penance for the slaughter at Hastings by building a great abbey
sentences.zh: 我们已经提到他如何通过建造一座伟大的修道院来为黑斯廷斯的屠杀赎罪，

sentences.en: on the site of the battle with the altar supposedly marking the place where Harold had made his last stand.
sentences.zh: 在战斗现场，祭坛据说是哈罗德最后一次抵抗的地方。

sentences.en: And according to Audric Fatalis, on his deathbed, he confessed that he had persecuted the people of England beyond all reason.
sentences.zh: 根据奥德里克·维塔利斯的说法，他在临终时承认，他毫无理由地迫害了英格兰人民。

sentences.en: But it is traumatic.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是创伤性的。

sentences.en: It's devastating, particularly if you're, you know, an Anglo-Saxon landowner.
sentences.zh: 这是毁灭性的，特别是如果你是一个盎格鲁-撒克逊土地所有者的话。

sentences.en: I mean, completely traumatic.
sentences.zh: 我是说，完全是创伤性的。

sentences.en: But I think it is something to put in the counterbalance that the Norman Conquest does end up bringing an end to many of
sentences.zh: 但我认为值得平衡的是，诺曼征服最终确实结束了我们在整个系列中描述的许多

sentences.en: the tribulations and evils that we have been describing over the course of this entire series.
sentences.zh: 苦难和邪恶。

sentences.en: So William's reign does effectively see the end of Viking invasions, of disputed successions, of feuding among rival magnates within the Kingdom of England.
sentences.zh: 所以威廉的统治确实有效地结束了维京人的入侵、王位继承纠纷、英格兰王国境内敌对权贵之间的争斗。

sentences.en: There's no equivalent of the rivalry between the Earls of Mercia and the Earls of Wessex.
sentences.zh: 没有相当于麦西亚伯爵和威塞克斯伯爵之间那种竞争的东西。

sentences.en: Both those ranks have gone.
sentences.zh: 这两个等级都已经消失了。

sentences.en: And more than that, I think it's a mistake to see the new regime that the conquest ushers in purely as characterized by brutality and greed.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，我认为将征服带来的新政权仅仅视为残暴和贪婪的特征是一个错误。

sentences.en: So Julian Rathbone in The Last
sentences.zh: 朱利安·拉斯伯恩在《最后的

sentences.en: English King compares the Normans to the Nazis in Poland.
sentences.zh: 英国国王》中将诺曼人比作波兰的纳粹。

sentences.en: I think that is grotesquely unfair on the Normans.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对诺曼人来说太不公平了。

sentences.en: I mean, they are fearsome adversaries, but they are also, and this may sound very strange to people, but they are the embodiments of a change in attitude towards victory
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们是可怕的对手，但他们也是，这听起来可能很奇怪，但他们是战争中对胜利和征服态度的转变的体现，

sentences.en: and conquest in war that will become hugely significant over the course of the centuries to come.
sentences.zh: 这种转变在未来的几个世纪里将变得非常重要。

sentences.en: So we talked about the possibility that William may personally have been involved in the butchery of Harold at Hastings, but possibly covered it up.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了威廉可能亲自参与了黑斯廷斯对哈罗德的屠杀，但可能掩盖了这一点的可能性。

sentences.en: And whether that's true or not is by the by.
sentences.zh: 无论这是真是假，都不重要。

sentences.en: That it can even be countenanced as a theory reflects the fact that the age when
sentences.zh: 它甚至可以被视为一种理论，反映了这样一个事实，即那个时代

sentences.en: slaughtering your enemies and cutting them up into pieces, and this could be praised, that this is fading
sentences.zh: 屠杀敌人并将他们切成碎片，这可以受到赞扬，正在消失

sentences.en: into history because the codes of what will become chivalry are already making their mark in France.
sentences.zh: 在历史中，因为将成为骑士精神的代码已经在法国留下了印记。

sentences.en: William does not actually slaughter large numbers of magnates.
sentences.zh: 威廉实际上并没有屠杀大量的权贵。

sentences.zh: 他唯一处决的人是

sentences.zh: 沃尔夫奥夫，诺森布里亚伯爵的儿子，他曾反抗过他。

sentences.en: Edgar Atheling, despite being implicated in countless insurrections, kind of lives to a ripe old age.
sentences.zh: 埃德加·阿瑟林尽管卷入了无数次起义，但还是活到了高龄。

sentences.en: He's the kind of the
sentences.zh: 他是那种

sentences.en: Richard Cromwell of Anglo-Saxon England.
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰的理查德·克伦威尔。

sentences.en: Even Stiggan.
sentences.zh: 即使是斯蒂根。

sentences.en: I mean, he's in prison, but he's not executed.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他被关进了监狱，但没有被处决。

sentences.en: And when Aldrich Vitalis condemns the harrowing of the North, he's judging it by William's own standards.
sentences.zh: 当奥德里克·维塔利斯谴责对北方的蹂躏时，他是在用威廉自己的标准来评判它。

sentences.en: The standards that had prevailed in the Anglo-Saxon period no longer prevail.
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊时期盛行的标准不再盛行。

sentences.en: It's no longer seen as acceptable to go around harrying entire counties.
sentences.zh: 到处蹂躏整个县不再被认为是可接受的。

sentences.en: You don't think that the Anglo-Saxon
sentences.zh: 你不认为《盎格鲁-撒克逊

sentences.zh: 编年史》会以同样的方式报道它，如果它是忏悔者爱德华或

sentences.zh: 埃塞尔雷德或其他人所做的吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle reports a lot of harrowings and ravagings.
sentences.zh: 我是说，《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》报道了很多蹂躏和破坏。

sentences.en: I mean, just to quote a really fascinating essay by Malcolm Strickland in a recent book of essays on the Norman ConqueSt. And he observes how in Britain and Scandinavia in the 11th
sentences.zh: 我是说，引用马尔科姆·斯特里克兰在最近一本关于诺曼征服的论文集中的一篇非常迷人的文章。他观察到在11世纪的英国和斯堪的纳维亚，

sentences.en: century.
sentences.zh: 世纪。

sentences.en: Enemy warriors were generally killed without quarter in combat or executed on capture, while women and children were enslaved.
sentences.zh: 敌方战士通常在战斗中被毫不留情地杀死或在被俘后被处决，而妇女和儿童则被奴役。

sentences.en: And any who might hinder the effective transport of this human booty, such as the old sick or very young, were put to the sword.
sentences.zh: 任何可能阻碍这种人类战利品有效运输的人，如老人、病人或非常年幼的人，都被处死。

sentences.en: By contrast, in Normandy, as in France, the enslaving of captives in wars between fellow Franks or other Christians had become regarded as unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，在诺曼底，就像在法国一样，在法兰克人或其他基督徒之间的战争中奴役俘虏已被视为不可接受。

sentences.en: And in that light, it's interesting to note that one of the most vivid social changes that is revealed by Doomsday Book is the decline of slavery.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，有趣的是，《末日审判书》揭示的最生动的社会变化之一是奴隶制的衰落。

sentences.en: We know that the English kings, the Anglo-Saxon kings, were absolutely in the habit of enslaving their enemies.
sentences.zh: 我们知道英国国王，盎格鲁-撒克逊国王，绝对有奴役敌人的习惯。

sentences.en: Bristol, long before it became a great centre for the Atlantic slave trade, was a massive booming entrepot for slaves who'd be exported to the caliphate or wherever.
sentences.zh: 布里斯托尔在成为大西洋奴隶贸易中心之前很久，就是一个巨大的、繁荣的奴隶转运港，这些奴隶会被出口到哈里发国或其他地方。

sentences.en: of England who lived as slaves, whereas William as king does take active steps to prohibit the slave trade.
sentences.zh: 而威廉作为国王确实采取了积极措施来禁止奴隶贸易。

sentences.zh: 所以威廉在某种意义上是英国历史上第一位伟大的废奴主义者。

sentences.zh: 我是说，这显然是一个激动人心的故事。

sentences.zh: 我们一直在强调这一点。

sentences.zh: 但我觉得它在道德层面也很复杂，这正是它如此迷人的原因。

sentences.en: Wonderful story, Tom.
sentences.zh: 精彩的故事，汤姆。

sentences.en: And brilliantly narrated.
sentences.zh: 叙述得也非常出色。

sentences.en: And also lurking behind all this, the notion of holy war, the idea that warriors can do God's purpose by felling their enemies, is the extraordinary story of the First Crusade.
